subject: Request to keep evaluation active during procurement slowdown
messages:
From: Katie Lawson <katie@veridianhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Eval window at risk — procurement review delaying PO

Hi Logan,

Quick heads-up: our finance and procurement teams are doing an internal review of third-party SaaS vendors and our purchase order for Redwood is still stuck in that queue. Procurement told me the earliest sign-off is ~2 weeks out because of an audit, so our shared sandbox/demo will run out before that unless we extend it.

We’ve made good progress — the clinicians on the trial are near the final validation step — and losing access mid-demo would be painful. Can Redwood keep the evaluation environment active for another 10 working days or provide a short-term credit to cover the next burst of usage?

I can share a screenshot of the PO status if that helps. Thanks for understanding.

—Katie
Katie Lawson
Director, Clinical Integrations
Veridian Health
[katie@veridianhealth.com]

Attachment: VERIDIAN_PO_STATUS.png

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Katie Lawson <katie@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Eval window at risk — procurement review delaying PO

Hi Katie — thanks for the heads-up and the context. Really glad the clinicians are close to sign-off.

We can absolutely help avoid a stop-gap in the evaluation. Operationally, I can provision a 10‑day environment hold or push a one-time trial credit to the account; for credits larger than $2k I’ll need quick approval from my manager (cc’d).

Two quick asks to speed approval:
- Can you confirm expected token/usage profile for the next 10 days (rough estimate of daily API calls or token volume)?
- Can you share the PO ETA from procurement (best guess)?

If you want, I can send a short addendum to extend the sandbox expiry by 10 days and note the PO tracking id.

I’ll await Marissa/Ben’s green light for credits.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: quick approval? Veridian needs short extension while PO clears

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Katie’s note. Veridian (DEAL-34921-V) has procurement paused for an audit; they asked for 10 working days to keep the eval live OR a short trial credit to get through clinician validation.

Suggested options (pick one):
1) Extend sandbox expiry by 10 calendar days (no billing change) — low friction, no docs.
2) Push a one-time $1,800 trial credit (covers anticipated usage for 10 days) — requires a small addendum.
3) Approve both (extend expiry + credit) if we want to minimize churn risk — requires manager sign-off on credit.

They look like solid fit; next milestone is clinical validation demo next week. I’ve asked Katie for a usage estimate but don’t want to wait to triage. If you approve option 2 or 3 I’ll prepare a one-page addendum and route for signature.

Deal context: ARR $120k, procurement hold seems procedural. HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-34921-V

—Logan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: quick approval? Veridian needs short extension while PO clears

Thanks for the context. Approve option 2 (one-time $1,800 trial credit) given the ARR and the stage — this is within our discretionary threshold for customer experience. Please attach the addendum that calls out the credit, expiration, and that the PO will be applied when received.

Please also include:
- Deal id in the addendum
- A line that the credit is non-recurring and applied as account credit only

I’ve uploaded a signed approval note to the deal record.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: approved_trial_addendum.pdf

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Katie Lawson <katie@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Eval window at risk — procurement review delaying PO

Hi Katie — good news. We’ve approved a one-time $1,800 trial credit to keep the evaluation running while your procurement review completes. I’ve attached a short addendum that documents the credit and the 10‑day extension window (see attached).

Next steps for you:
- I attached the addendum (PDF) — please confirm receipt and that you’re OK with the wording.
- If you can share a quick estimate of expected daily API calls, I’ll monitor usage and top up if we see unexpected spikes.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-34921-V

Attachment: approved_trial_addendum.pdf

Thanks and we’ll keep an eye on this so there’s no interruption during your validation.

—Logan

From: Katie Lawson <katie@veridianhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Eval window at risk — procurement review delaying PO

Logan — got the addendum and the credit applied. Thank you — that removed a lot of stress for the clinical team. Procurement now expects PO sign-off early next week; I’ll forward the PO as soon as it’s issued. Appreciate the quick turnaround from you and Marissa.

—Katie
